title: Cross-carrier predictive automata
purpose: Separate current/public matching from future-sufficient predictive structure on two disjoint carrier tokens.
carriers: Distinct tokens X_S and X_T, each with four states; carrier identity is declared before any bridge verdict.
states: X_S={s_(o,h): o,h∈{0,1}} and X_T={t_(o,h): o,h∈{0,1}}.  The current lens returns o; the hidden memory coordinate h is not in the current record.
inputs: U={tick,flip}; public trials may use tick at the handoff state, while the predictive probe family includes words of length at most two over both inputs.
transition: tick sends (o,h)↦(h,h); flip sends (o,h)↦(o,1-h).  The positive target has the same typed law under φ(s_(o,h))=t_(o,h).  The counterfeit target replaces tick by (o,h)↦(0,h).
interfaces: Current lens L(o,h)=o; predictive trace probe Π_H records L along every input word of length ≤2.  Thus s_(0,0) and s_(0,1) are current-equal but predictive-distinct.
bridge: Positive bridge R_+=graph(φ), with identity input map and stage-local clock map.  Counterfeit bridge R_- collapses h before target initialization.
positive_witness: R_+ is saturated for the predictive equivalence and induces a quotient bisimulation; exact target carrier and source carrier remain distinct tokens.
negative_control: R_- preserves the handoff public record o=0 but fails the length-one tick probe for h=1.  A public-only criterion returns a false positive.
expected_witnesses: Predictive partition; saturated relation; one distinguishing input word; quotient transition table; exact failure pair.
controls: Same-carrier relabeling control; target with an extra unreachable state; target with public equality but hidden-transition mismatch.
separates: SF-03 from public-shadow criteria; TS-01/TS-09 from behavior-only candidates; provides a hidden-structure clause test for SF-01.
family_roles: SF-01=component/control;SF-02=outside endpoint control;SF-03=core positive and counterfeit
minimality: Four states are the smallest convenient deterministic product exposing one current bit and one future-relevant hidden bit without identifying carrier tokens.
formalization: Finite types, total transition functions, bounded words, equivalence relations, and relational saturation; exact booleans only.
kill_condition: The chosen predictive probes fail to distinguish the counterfeit, or the bridge definition already requires quotient equality rather than checking it.
nonclaim: Predictive equivalence alone is not a full C-package, lineage, autonomy, consciousness, or personal identity result.

title: Gradual mixed-support handoff
purpose: Give SF-02 a noncircular positive control and give SF-01 a staged target-ownership test.
carriers: Source modules S0,S1 and target modules T0,T1 are four separately named support tokens.
states: Process state q∈{0,1}; at each stage a support set A_k and two contribution bits c_k^a,c_k^b determine q_(k+1)=q_k xor c_k^a xor c_k^b.
inputs: One endogenous update input step plus an allowed disturbance bit d∈{0,1}; all values are finite and explicit.
transition: Stage 0 uses {S0,S1}; stage 1 uses {S1,T0}; stage 2 uses {T0,T1}; stage 3 uses {T0,T1} after source withdrawal.  At stage 1 both S1 and T0 are nonredundant: fixing either contribution changes q_(2).
interfaces: The operational event DAG records support ownership, causal parents, process signature q, local clock k, and a responsibility frontier.  No edge is labeled lineage in advance.
bridge: A corridor is the sequence A_0…A_3 plus signature-preserving update maps, one mixed nonredundant stage, no empty process stage, and target takeover at stage 2.
positive_witness: The finite corridor connects source-only support to target-only support, preserves q, contains a genuine mixed update, and remains defined after source/controller withdrawal.
negative_control: Use identical endpoint states but replace stage 1 by source termination followed by target initialization from a static record; the mixed-step predicate and overlap corridor fail.
expected_witnesses: Stage table; causal DAG; nonredundancy certificates for both sides; no-gap trace; target-only invariant cycle.
controls: Pure source update; pure target update; bridge-controller-dependent target; same endpoint without mixed stage.
separates: SF-02 from endpoint and ancestry-only views; SF-01 autonomy from bridge-supported behavior; SF-03 may still classify the negative control as ancestry when provenance exists.
minimality: Two modules per side are needed to exhibit a nontrivial mixed replacement stage rather than a single edge relabeled as overlap.
formalization: Finite stage index, support subsets, Boolean influence/nonredundancy checks, event DAG reachability, and relation composition.
kill_condition: The mixed-step condition is either vacuous, depends on the desired lineage verdict, or does not survive concatenation of two valid corridors.
nonclaim: The model does not show that causal overlap is necessary for consciousness or that its structural lineage is numerical identity.

title: Destructive reconstruction with operational provenance
purpose: Force the live-process and relation-valued ancestry families to disagree on an exact, source-derived reconstruction.
carriers: One two-state source token X_S, one two-state target token X_T, and one finite record token R; all are distinct.
states: Source and target states q∈{0,1}; record r∈{0,1,empty}; source active flag a_S and target active flag a_T.
transition: snapshot copies q_S into r; erase sets a_S=0; after an explicit one-step gap activate sets q_T=r and a_T=1.  No stage has active source and target process support simultaneously.
interfaces: Operational graph contains X_S→R→X_T data-dependence edges and timestamps; an independently built twin X_T' has the same state law but no path from X_S.
bridge: The record transform is exact and source-derived.  It is a valid structural translation and a candidate ancestry seed, but it is not a mixed-support overlap corridor.
positive_witness: SF-03 can relate X_S to X_T through the explicit provenance seed and transition closure; target structure can be exact.
negative_control: X_T' is initialized to the same q without a source-derived path.  SF-03 must exclude it under no-ex-nihilo closure; SF-02 rejects both reconstructions as overlap lineage.
expected_witnesses: Operational provenance path; exact state transform; explicit empty interval; independent-twin nonreachability proof.
controls: No erase; zero-gap but no overlap; stale record; two targets initialized from the same record.
separates: SF-02 versus SF-03; target realization versus lineage; exact copying versus source-derived ancestry.
family_roles: SF-01=target-realization only;SF-02=negative control;SF-03=positive ancestry with twin negative
minimality: A two-state source, one record, and one target suffice to expose the gap, provenance path, and independent-twin distinction.
formalization: Finite labeled transition system, reachability, least fixed point on a relation, and an explicit gap predicate.
kill_condition: The ancestry seed cannot be stated operationally without using the term continuation, or closure relates the independent twin despite no source path.
nonclaim: Source-derived reconstruction is not thereby personal survival, and overlap rejection is not a proof of phenomenal discontinuity.

title: Exact symmetric duplication
purpose: Make unique continuation impossible under exact target symmetry while preserving relation-valued branch outputs.
carriers: One source token X_S and two target tokens X_A,X_B with disjoint but isomorphic two-state carriers.
states: Each target has q∈{0,1}, the same transition table, the same source-derived initialization record, and the same target-local resources.
inputs: copy,tick plus a target-swap automorphism σ exchanging every A-labeled datum with its B-labeled counterpart.
transition: Both targets are initialized by identical source-derived transforms and run independently under the same deterministic law.
interfaces: Every admitted source-relative observable, provenance label modulo target token, package witness, and performance trace is fixed by σ except for exchanging A and B.
bridge: Two isomorphic bridge branches B_A and B_B; neither contains an admissible asymmetry.
positive_witness: Relation-valued ancestry or process fission may return {(S,A),(S,B)}.  The witness is invariant under σ.
negative_control: Any rule returning exactly one target violates σ-invariance unless an additional asymmetry is declared and audited.
expected_witnesses: Explicit automorphism; two qualifying branch certificates; selector contradiction trace.
controls: Add a genuine asymmetric causal path; delete one target after copying; distinguish target resources only after the selection point.
separates: Relation-valued SF-02/SF-03 outputs from unique-selector readings; demonstrates that later deletion does not retroactively create uniqueness.
family_roles: SF-01=two target packages no selection;SF-02=branch-valued if genuine fork;SF-03=two successors
minimality: One source and two isomorphic two-state targets are sufficient for a nontrivial target-exchange automorphism.
formalization: Finite permutations, invariant predicates, relations, and contradiction by applying σ to a unique selected token.
kill_condition: The model accidentally contains an admissible asymmetry, or the selector is allowed to use unregistered target names.
nonclaim: The symmetry theorem does not decide whether both, neither, or only a relation-valued pair should count phenomenally.

title: Public-perfect hidden/package counterfeit
purpose: Show that report equality and even a shallow certificate can coexist with a predictive, binding, or target-ownership failure.
carriers: Positive target X_T+ and counterfeit X_T- are distinct eight-state systems with the same public interface alphabet.
states: State=(r,h,b), r,h,b∈{0,1}; r is report, h is hidden predictive memory, b is a binding parity bit.  A certificate surface reports only r and a declared checksum c=r.
inputs: report,probe,bind.  The admitted public channel exposes report only; internal audit probes can use probe and bind.
transition: Positive target updates r←h on probe and b←r xor h on bind.  Counterfeit preserves every report command but fixes h=0 after handoff or sets b=0 independently.
interfaces: Public/report traces and shallow certificate c agree at the handoff and under report commands; predictive and joint-binding probes distinguish the systems.
bridge: Both receive the same public initialization.  Only the positive bridge carries and target-internalizes h and the binding law.
positive_witness: Internal probe suite recovers the expected predictive partition and binding parity on X_T+.
negative_control: X_T- passes public/report equality and the shallow certificate but fails at least one hidden package obligation.
expected_witnesses: Public trace equality; one hidden distinguishing word; one joint-binding mismatch; certificate/pass-versus-package/fail table.
controls: Expose h publicly; remove binding from the package; use a complete finite interface and demonstrate that the no-go premise then fails.
separates: SF-01 integrated package from report/certificate matching; SF-03 predictive ancestry from public equivalence; recognition lane from structural truth.
minimality: Three Boolean coordinates suffice to separate report, predictive memory, and joint binding without a large simulation.
formalization: Finite products, projection lenses, bounded traces, parity, and independent predicates.
kill_condition: The declared public interface already contains every differentiating probe, or the counterfeit differs only by an unregistered property.
nonclaim: The hidden or binding coordinate is a structural control, not a proof that the coordinate is consciousness-constitutive.

title: Fission, fusion, and recombination parity
purpose: Separate branchwise preservation from joint recombination and expose fusion conflicts in exclusive action-credit histories.
carriers: A four-state joint source X_S, two two-state branch carriers X_A,X_B, and a four-state fused target X_F.
states: Source state=(x,y)∈{0,1}² with joint invariant p=x xor y.  Branch A carries x and credit label α; branch B carries y and exclusive credit label β.
transition: split projects to x and y.  Positive recombination returns (x,y,p=x xor y).  Counterfeit recombination returns the same marginals but p=0.  A fused exclusive-credit field cannot simultaneously equal α and β when α≠β.
interfaces: Branch interfaces expose only their marginal bit and local credit label; a recombination probe exposes p and a fusion audit requests one coherent credit law.
bridge: Projection branches plus a typed recombination map; fusion is admissible only with a declared conflict-resolution function for credit.
positive_witness: Both branches preserve marginals and the positive fused target preserves parity with a nonexclusive provenance set {α,β}.
negative_control: Counterfeit has identical branch data but wrong parity, or claims one exclusive credit owner while both histories remain active.
expected_witnesses: Marginal equality table; parity counterexample; branch relation; fusion provenance/conflict record.
controls: Factorizable joint invariant; equal credit labels; branch deletion before fusion; no recombination probe.
separates: SF-03 relation-valued fission/fusion from pairwise matching; SF-01 global binding/gluing; SF-02 genuine process fork/merge from endpoint aggregation.
family_roles: SF-01=global package control;SF-02=process fork/fusion control;SF-03=core relation-valued positive
minimality: Two binary branch variables are the smallest classical construction with identical marginals and a nontrivial joint parity witness.
formalization: Finite products, projections, XOR, relations, and a partial fusion operation guarded by a conflict predicate.
kill_condition: All admitted joint probes factor through marginals, or fusion credit is defined so weakly that incompatible exclusive claims never conflict.
nonclaim: Recombination preservation and provenance consistency do not establish consciousness or personal identity after fission/fusion.

title: Integrated package with bridge-removal autonomy
purpose: Supply SF-01 with one exact finite positive package and a behavior-matched decoder/scheduler shadow that fails target ownership after withdrawal.
carriers: Source X_S, autonomous target X_T+, shadow target X_T-, external decoder D, scheduler C, and repair service R are separately individuated tokens.
states: Target local state=(q,h,a,k,z,v)∈{0,1}^6 with fixed self token self=T. q=public state, h=hidden predictive memory, a=action/credit bit, k=local clock mod 2, z=binding parity, v=viability bit.
inputs: sense,act,disturb,withdraw.  Allowed disturbances flip v from 1 to 0 once per maintenance cycle.
transition: Autonomous target computes q' from h, updates a from its own selected action, increments k locally, sets z=q xor h, and repairs v to 1.  Shadow target obtains the h update from D, clock from C, and repair from R; after withdraw it enters sink ⊥ within one cycle.
interfaces: Public lens exposes q and report; internal audit exposes typed witnesses: nonpublic h affecting futures, self=T, action-causal dependence, local clock ownership, parity z, and invariant viable set K={v=1 plus one repair-pending state}.
bridge: Staged bridge transports or rebuilds the six local coordinates, records all ownership dependencies, glues clause witnesses on their overlaps, then removes X_S,D,C,R and the migration controller.
positive_witness: X_T+ satisfies the eight finite clause proxies: closed object, nonfactorable promoted h, endogenous self-coordinate, interface-relative nonexposure, action credit, target-local time, joint binding, and post-disturbance viability.  All witnesses remain target-owned after withdrawal.
negative_control: X_T- produces the same supported public traces and certificate fields for three cycles but fails the ownership/gluing ledger and reaches ⊥ after withdrawal.
expected_witnesses: Eight clause records; overlap/join table; dependency ownership graph; withdrawal trace; invariant-set certificate; shadow collapse trace.
controls: Internalize only D; internalize only scheduler; no disturbance; externally hosted but target-owned resource under an explicitly enlarged carrier boundary.
separates: SF-01 from public/certificate matching and encoded-but-decoder-dependent migration; gives SF-02/SF-03 an independent target-realization/autonomy module.
family_roles: SF-01=defining positive and shadow negative;SF-02=autonomy module;SF-03=autonomy outside ancestry
minimality: Six variable coordinates plus a fixed self token are the smallest explicit product used here to keep predictive, credit, time, binding, and viability obligations independently falsifiable; objecthood and strict promotion are properties of the same finite dynamics.
formalization: Finite product type, clause predicates, ownership labels, acyclic overlap hypergraph, sink state, invariant-set reachability, and exact withdrawal operation.
kill_condition: The positive package passes only because one clause is defined in terms of the overall success predicate, or the shadow cannot be behavior-matched before withdrawal.
nonclaim: The finite clause proxies are a structural surrogate.  Passing them does not prove certificate soundness, consciousness, lineage, survival, or A2.

title: Route holonomy and bridge-composition defect
purpose: Show that identical endpoints and locally valid bridges need not determine one route-independent transported object.
carriers: Four carrier-stage tokens S,A,B,T arranged as a square with routes S→A→T and S→B→T.
states: Retained object=(q,m)∈{0,1}², where q is public endpoint state and m is route memory.
inputs: edge traversal and a closed-loop audit.
transition: Every edge preserves q.  Edges through A preserve m; edge B→T flips m.  Reverse edges are defined so the loop S→B→T→A→S flips m exactly once.
interfaces: Endpoint public lens sees q only; route audit sees edge sequence and m.  Direct bridge S→T is declared to preserve m.
bridge: Each edge map is typed and locally admissible.  The two composite routes disagree on m, and one composite disagrees with the direct bridge.
positive_witness: In the flat control obtained by removing the flip, cycle-basis holonomy is identity and all path transports agree.
negative_control: With the flip, endpoints/public traces agree while loop action and composite bridge differ.
expected_witnesses: Cycle basis; edge-map matrices/tables; path transport comparison; nontrivial loop witness; direct-versus-composite mismatch.
controls: Include m in the endpoint public interface; quotient m away deliberately; add a compensating flip on another edge.
separates: Every survivor's route-independent strengthening from route-indexed semantics; tests TS-07/TS-06 and bridge composition.
family_roles: SF-01=gluing/route gate;SF-02=process-route composition gate;SF-03=route-indexed ancestry gate
minimality: A square is the smallest route graph with two distinct simple paths between the same endpoints and a nontrivial cycle.
formalization: Finite graph, edge functions, path fold, cycle basis, equality of endomaps, and relational bridge composition.
kill_condition: Route memory is excluded by definition without justification, or the path-comparison theorem assumes flatness as endpoint equality.
nonclaim: Nontrivial holonomy does not by itself imply loss of consciousness or personal identity; it blocks unqualified route independence for the retained object.

title: Vector residual and local hard-gate counterfeit
purpose: Distinguish typed local adequacy from a favorable scalar average and provide exact rational stability/counterexample cases.
carriers: Source and target each carry four audited coordinates: predictive p, binding b, temporal t, and viability v.
states: Defect vector d=(d_p,d_b,d_t,d_v)∈{0,1/100,1/10,1}^4 with exact rational values; hard gate g_v requires d_v=0 in the first landing.
inputs: one bridge stage, two-stage composition, and a withdrawal disturbance.
transition: Positive bridge has d=(1/100,1/100,0,0) with margins (1/10,1/10,1/10,1).  Counterfeit has d=(0,0,0,1) but scalar average (d_p+d_b+d_t+d_v)/100=1/100 under a deliberately tiny viability weight.
interfaces: Auditor reports both the vector/local maxima and any scalar summary.  Hard gates are evaluated before aggregation.
bridge: Exact defect records compose by declared coordinatewise bound d(B2∘B1)≤d(B1)+d(B2); no bound is assumed without a proof for the selected metric.
positive_witness: All local defects remain below margins and every hard gate passes under one- and two-stage exact rational bounds.
negative_control: Scalar score passes while the viability coordinate crosses its hard gate; a second control accumulates two subthreshold route defects past a margin.
expected_witnesses: Exact residual vector; margin table; hard-gate failure; scalar false-positive certificate; composition arithmetic.
controls: Uniform weights; no hard gates; margin exactly zero; a metric whose composition law is not subadditive.
separates: TS-09 layer from scalar similarity; SF-01 package stability from average fidelity; SF-03 approximate ancestry from untyped closeness.
minimality: Four coordinates are enough to keep one viability-critical defect independent of three favorable coordinates; exact rational weights prevent floating ambiguity.
formalization: Vectors over rationals, coordinatewise order, finite horizons, explicit margins, and decidable hard gates.
kill_condition: No nontrivial stability margin can be stated, or the metric/composition law is chosen after seeing the desired verdict.
nonclaim: Residual bounds do not identify the correct consciousness-relevant metric and do not license approximate personal identity.

title: Viability threshold and endogenous repair
purpose: Give exact positive and negative autonomy cases near a maintained closure boundary.
carriers: One source and two target variants with identical nominal output laws but different target-owned repair resources.
states: Health state H={safe,warning,failed}; budget b∈{0,1}; viable set K={(safe,b),(warning,1)}.
transition: hit sends safe→warning and warning→failed.  A target-owned repair with b=1 sends warning→safe and consumes then regenerates b on the next safe tick.  The boundary target lacks regeneration after withdrawal.
interfaces: Public output is identical in safe and warning.  Autonomy audit observes target-owned transition/resource graph and all allowed disturbance sequences with at most one hit per two ticks.
bridge: Handoff ends in warning with b=1.  Positive target remains in K under the declared disturbance class; negative target reaches failed after withdrawal because repair or budget regeneration was external.
positive_witness: A finite invariant-set certificate for K and an explicit repair cycle using target resources only.
negative_control: Same handoff state and supported behavior, but post-withdrawal reachability contains failed; a near-boundary perturbation also shows no uniform theorem at zero margin.
expected_witnesses: Maximal controlled-invariant subset; withdrawal reachability tree; resource ownership record; boundary counterexample.
controls: No disturbances; unlimited external repair; enlarged target boundary that legitimately includes the repair module; stale repair budget.
separates: SF-01/SF-02 autonomy claims from supported behavior; tests the viability module independently of lineage.
family_roles: SF-01=autonomy positive/negative;SF-02=mandatory autonomy gate;SF-03=outside ancestry conclusion
minimality: Three health states distinguish interior, repairable boundary, and failure; one budget bit makes repair ownership nontrivial.
formalization: Finite controlled transition relation, disturbance language, greatest fixed point for K, and exact reachability.
kill_condition: The disturbance class is tuned to guarantee the result, or the repair resource remains outside the declared target boundary.
nonclaim: Viability is one structural obligation and is neither sufficient for the full C-package nor evidence of personal identity.
